Title: Display Apple Pay for a cart with an eligible item
Preconditions: Apple Pay is enabled in the test environment; the test catalog has an item confirmed eligible for Apple Pay.
Test Data: One preconfigured eligible test item; no real customer data.
Steps: 1. Open the storefront as a shopper. 2. Add the eligible item to the cart. 3. Open the Cart page. 4. Inspect the express payment area.
Expected Result: An Apple Pay express payment button is displayed on the Cart page.
Postconditions / Cleanup: Remove the test item from the cart.
Automation Candidate: Yes: stable cart state and visible button can be checked in UI automation.
Notes: Eligibility rules and an authoritative eligible-item fixture are not defined; see GAP-1.

Title: Hide express payment buttons for an empty cart
Preconditions: The storefront is available and the cart is empty.
Steps: 1. Open the Cart page with no items in the cart. 2. Inspect the express payment area.
Expected Result: No express payment button is displayed while the cart is empty.

Title: Pass the cart order total to the Apple Pay sheet
Preconditions: Apple Pay is enabled; a test cart has a non-zero item subtotal, shipping, tax, and discount; the Cart page displays its order total.
Test Data: Preconfigured test cart and provider sandbox; record the exact total shown on the Cart page before opening the sheet.
Steps: 1. Open the Cart page. 2. Record the displayed order total and confirm the cart has non-zero item, shipping, tax, and discount amounts. 3. Click the Apple Pay button. 4. Read the amount shown in the provider payment sheet without authorizing.
Expected Result: The provider payment sheet opens and its amount exactly matches the order total displayed on the Cart page, including the cart's items, shipping, tax, and discounts.
Postconditions / Cleanup: Cancel the payment sheet and confirm no order was placed.
Automation Candidate: Later: provider sandbox and stable cart quote are required.
Notes: Ticket does not specify tax/discount calculation rules; compare with the authoritative cart total rather than assuming a formula.

Title: Return to an unchanged cart after cancelling express payment
Preconditions: Apple Pay is enabled and a provider payment sheet can be opened; cart contains an eligible item.
Test Data: Capture cart items, quantities, and displayed totals before opening the sheet.
Steps: 1. Open the Cart page and record its items, quantities, and totals. 2. Click the Apple Pay button. 3. Cancel or close the provider payment sheet. 4. Reopen or inspect the Cart page.
Expected Result: The shopper returns to the Cart page; cart items, quantities, and totals are unchanged; no order is created.
Postconditions / Cleanup: Leave the original cart available for subsequent tests or remove its item.
Automation Candidate: Yes: compare the cart state before and after cancellation.

Title: Show a payment error without creating an order on decline
Preconditions: Apple Pay is enabled and the provider sandbox can simulate a declined or failed payment; cart contains an eligible item.
Test Data: Eligible test item; provider sandbox decline/failure response.
Steps: 1. Record the cart state. 2. Click the Apple Pay button. 3. Trigger a declined or failed payment in the provider sandbox. 4. Observe the message and verify whether an order exists.
Expected Result: An error message is shown and no order is created.
Postconditions / Cleanup: Keep the cart unchanged for inspection, then clean up test data.
Automation Candidate: Later: failure simulation and order lookup are needed.
Notes: The ticket requires an error message but does not define its text, placement, or recovery action.
